conceptExplanation: Select the exact Board package and USB Serial Port (COMx on Windows, /dev/cu.* on macOS, /dev/ttyUSB0 or /dev/ttyACM0 on Linux) before uploading.

lessons.title: Troubleshooting
lessons.introduction: Diagnose the 5 most common Arduino IDE issues systematically: charge-only USB cables, missing CH340/CP2102 drivers, wrong Board/Port, Old Bootloader on Nano clones, and busy COM ports.
objectives: Understand troubleshooting in Arduino IDE 2.x.
Follow reliable verification and hardware safety habits.
Diagnose common beginner IDE issues independently.
conceptExplanation: Diagnose the 5 most common Arduino IDE issues systematically: charge-only USB cables, missing CH340/CP2102 drivers, wrong Board/Port, Old Bootloader on Nano clones, and busy COM ports.

Never panic when upload fails! Check in order: (1) Data-capable USB cable, (2) Board & Processor selection, (3) Active Port, (4) Close any other app using the serial port, (5) Disconnect wires from D0/D1 on Uno/Nano.
lessons.analogy: Troubleshooting is a checklist, not guesswork — rule out physical cable and port issues before blaming your code.
